newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey welcomes EU-inspired talks with Greece.
newsitem.headline: Turkey welcomes EU-inspired talks with Greece.

text.p: Turkey said on Wednesday it welcomed an EU-inspired mediation meeting with neighbour Greece scheduled to take place later this month in the Netherlands.
"It is envisaged that the first meeting will be held in the middle of the month in the Netherlands," foreign ministry spokesman Sermet Atacanli told a news briefing.
"We hope the committee's work will be a positive and constructive start for solving the problems," he said.
The Netherlands, currently holding the EU presidency, will bring together two non-governmental representatives from both sides at the meeting.
Greece, a member of the Europen Union, has vetoed EU funds to Turkey and blocks many of Ankara's efforts to get closer to the 15-nation group.
NATO allies Turkey and Greece are at odds over the divided island of Cyprus, territory in the Aegean Sea and minority rights.
They nearly went to war last year over two uninhabited islets in the eastern Aegean. A clash was averted with last-minute U.S. intervention.
Ankara has repeatedly called for a direct dialogue to resolve differences but Athens says this would suggest Greece's borders were open to negotiations.
Atacanli said the experts would prepare a report on the disputes and submit it to Ankara and Athens by mid-June. Both governments are not bound by the report, he said.
